title: Chapter 11 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of anti‑forensics: data hiding, trail obfuscation, artifact wiping, and detection countermeasures.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of anti‑forensics?
options: To make digital investigations more difficult or impossible
questions.explanation: Anti‑forensics aims to hinder or prevent the recovery of digital evidence.

questions.question: Which NTFS attribute is more resistant to timestomping because it is set by the kernel?
questions.explanation: $FILE_NAME timestamps are harder to tamper with than $STANDARD_INFORMATION.

questions.question: Encrypting a file is a form of anti‑forensics because it hinders analysis.
questions.explanation: Encryption obscures content, making forensic examination impossible without the key.

questions.question: The Windows command `cipher /w:C:` is used to wipe ___ on drive C:.
questions.explanation: `cipher /w:C:` overwrites free space to destroy deleted file remnants.

questions.question: What is a forensic indicator that CCleaner was used on a system?
questions.explanation: Prefetch files record program execution, even if the executable is later deleted.

questions.question: What is the main challenge with secure deletion on SSDs?
options: Wear leveling may leave old data in stale pages despite overwrite
questions.explanation: The FTL remaps logical addresses, so overwriting a logical address may not overwrite the physical page containing the original data.

questions.question: Steganography hides the content of a message, while encryption hides its existence.
questions.explanation: It's the opposite: encryption hides content, steganography hides existence.

questions.question: A VeraCrypt hidden volume provides ___ deniability.
questions.explanation: The hidden volume is designed so its existence cannot be proven, allowing the user to plausibly deny its existence.

questions.question: Which Event ID indicates that the Windows Security log was cleared?
questions.explanation: Event 1102 is generated when the Security log is cleared.

questions.question: How can memory forensics defeat full‑disk encryption?
options: By capturing the encryption keys that reside in RAM while the volume is unlocked
questions.explanation: Encryption keys are present in memory when the drive is mounted; a memory dump can extract them.

questions.question: Unallocated space filled with all zeros is a strong sign of free space wiping.
questions.explanation: Normal unallocated space contains random remnants; uniform patterns indicate intentional overwrite.

questions.question: The tool ___ can be used to detect steganography in images by statistical analysis.
questions.explanation: StegExpose analyzes LSB and other steganographic methods to score suspicion.

questions.question: What does timestomping refer to?
options: Manipulating file MAC timestamps to mislead investigators
questions.explanation: Timestomping alters the recorded file times to confuse timeline analysis.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an anti‑forensic technique?
options: Using a write‑blocker to image a drive
Encrypting a hard drive with BitLocker
Using timestomp to change file creation times
questions.explanation: Using a write‑blocker is a forensic best practice, not an anti‑forensic method.

questions.question: If the Windows Event Log is cleared, the event 1102 can never be deleted.
questions.explanation: Attackers can also clear or prevent event 1102 from being logged through advanced memory manipulation.

questions.question: PowerShell script block logging records executed commands in Event ID ___.
questions.explanation: Script block logging (4104) captures full PowerShell command text.

questions.question: What is the best forensic defense against timestomping?
options: Comparing timestamps from multiple sources ($SI, $FN, USN Journal)
questions.explanation: Cross‑referencing different timestamp sources can reveal discrepancies caused by stomping.

questions.question: Why might a 10 GB VeraCrypt container with only 2 GB of visible data be suspicious?
options: It indicates the container is corrupted
It could indicate a hidden volume inside the container
It means VeraCrypt failed to encrypt properly
It means the data was deleted
questions.explanation: The remaining space could be a hidden volume; the outer volume shows only 2 GB to mask the hidden one.

questions.question: Volume Shadow Copies can be a source of files that were later securely deleted.
questions.explanation: VSS snapshots preserve previous versions, so even if the current file is wiped, an older snapshot may still have it.

questions.question: Which of the following is an anti‑forensic tool used for file shredding?
questions.explanation: Eraser is a tool that securely overwrites files to prevent recovery.
